Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 82, verse 1:

(p-298) Surat al-Infitar (The Cleaving)

Its purpose is to warn against immersion in evil deeds, deceived by the Lord's beneficence and generosity and forgetful of the Day of Religion (yawm al-din), on which one is called to account for the smallest speck (naqir) and the thinnest membrane (qitmir), and on which no soul can avail another soul at all. Its name, al-Infitar, is the clearest indication of this.

(In the name of Allah) whose is majesty as well as beauty. (The Most Gracious) who encompasses all with mercy, so that one would give thanks, yet this deceived the people of misguidance. (The Most Merciful) who singles out whomever He wills with success in the qualities He is pleased with.

* *

When al-Takwir was concluded with the statement that He, glorified is He, does not go beyond His will, and that He is the Originator of creation and its Manager, and some people believed that this world is as it is, with no end ("wombs push out, the earth swallows, and whoever dies is gone and turns to dust, and there is no return after the loss"), Allah, glorified is He, opened this surah with what serves as an introduction to the purpose of the preceding one, namely that this world must necessarily be dismantled and ruined so that He may call people to account, recompensing each of them, the good-doer and the wrongdoer, for what they did. So He said: ﴿When the sky is cleft asunder﴾, meaning, despite its firm construction, its harmony, and its good order, ﴿ruptured﴾ (p-299), meaning split into fissures, which the context of awe makes clear, so that its gates acquire many sides, and thereby lose the cohesive sphere of air in which people live like fish in water. Just as when water is withdrawn from sea creatures they perish, so too will the air be with land creatures. Then there will be no life except through a new raising and a transfer from these causes, so that reckoning may take place through reward and punishment.

When the sky has been split apart, its fastening loosened and its hold on what was fixed in it gone, so that this would be a stronger warning to those beneath it, since they would be watching constantly for its fall or for the fall of some part of it upon them, leaving them with no place of settled rest, [he said]: ﴿And when the stars are scattered﴾. That is, the stars, small and large, all of them, the bright, shining, blazing ones, which are kindled like lamps set with nails in fastened things, by which God has arranged in this abode of causes the four seasons, the night and the day, and other great purposes. They were preserved by the orderliness of the sky. ﴿They are scattered﴾, that is, they fall in disarray, just as pearls fall from a string when it breaks, falling with such speed that, because of the strength of their tendency to fall, they need no agent to make them fall.

When the report of what indicates the heavens (which are the sky) was given with [a hint -] of the scattering of the earth, because the earth is more perfect and more honourable than them, since it stands to the earth as the male does to the female, and since being acted upon may perhaps give the impression that this happens without an agent, [Allah] stated the scattering of the earth explicitly, using the passive voice to indicate that the whole matter is by His act and that this is easy for Him. So He said, informing of the splitting of the lands as well, so as to combine the frightening with the reassuring in brief: ﴿And when the seas﴾ (the scattered bodies of water upon the earth, which He has regulated with the utmost regulation for the benefit of the servants despite their abundance), ﴿are set ablaze﴾ (i.e., a great kindling), by the removal of the barriers that were between them; and al-Rabi' said: by their overflowing and the water of them going beyond its limits, so that some of them mix with others, their salt mixing with their fresh water, and they become one sea, so that the whole earth becomes water, and there is no sky and no earth, so where is the escape?

Since that (the scattering of the stars and the other events of the preceding verses) would bring about the overturning of the graves, it might give the impression that their people would not rise again, as the Arabs used to believe that whoever dies is gone for good. So, to repel this, he said, in the manner of the speech of those who are able (to do something), indicating how easy that is for Him: ﴿And when the graves are overturned﴾, meaning, despite all of that, ﴿are scattered﴾, meaning their dirt is dug up in the easiest manner, so their people are brought out from them, and they rise alive as they were, and then they see what horrified them, frightened them and terrified them.

When all these signs that were made indicators of the Hour were entailing subtle knowledge, each one of them revealing wondrous matters, and they were all indicating the transition from this abode to another abode because of the ruin of this abode, it was fitting that "idha" (when) be answered by His saying: ﴿a soul will know﴾, i.e., all souls, with the news of the reckoning and of what He, glory be to Him, will make for it by the strength of the composition from a faculty of recollection, as He, exalted, said: ﴿So We have removed from you your covering﴾ [Qaf: 22]. What indicates the intention of generality is the indefinite expression in the context of warning and caution, together with the knowledge that all souls are alike, in knowing such a thing and in ignorance of it, in one degree. Whatever is established for the resurrection is established for all. Perhaps he used the indefinite as an indication that whoever God has granted intellect should consider that it is he who is meant, and so fear: ﴿what it has sent forward﴾, i.e., of deeds, ﴿and what it has left behind﴾, i.e., all that it did of good or evil or other, or what it sent forward before death and what it left behind of a sunna (a practice or precedent) that remains after it.

[p-301]

Imam Abu Ja'far Ibn al-Zubayr said: This surah is as if it were part of the completion of Surat al-Takwir, because of the unity of purpose; its connection to it is clear. A parallel to this has passed. End of quote.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 82, verse 6:

When that (the preceding description of the Day of Judgment) was heart-rending, and a person who believes in the Resurrection may, out of heedlessness toward some sins, say: "My return is to the Generous, and He will do nothing to me but good," (the speech) was made to come with the particle of distance (ya, in calling "O") because most of creation, despite that, is exposed (to the danger), denouncing, glorified and exalted is He, those who say this, being deceived by the delusions of Satan, with a denunciation that shakes the pillars: ﴿O mankind (al-insan)﴾, that is, the human race (al-bashar), the one at ease with himself and forgetful of what concerns him. ﴿What has deceived you﴾, that is, what has brought you into delusion (al-ghirrah), which is to see your ugly deed as good, or to think that you will certainly be pardoned for it. This carries the same sense as the reading of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-A'mash: "aghurraka" with the hamzah of denial, while the well-known reading adds the sense of wonder. ﴿by your Lord﴾, that is, the One who does good to you, whose goodness made you forget that you were created for the salvation of your soul through doing what He legislated for you.

Since the expression "the Lord" (al-Rabb), together with its indication of goodness, also indicates retribution when one persists in crime, because that is the manner of the one who nurtures, this served as a barrier against delusion for whoever reflects. He then followed it with something of the same nature, whose outward aspect is gentleness and whose inward aspect is majesty and subjugation, saying, for emphasis in preventing delusion:

﴿the Generous﴾, that is, the One to whom all perfection belongs, which requires that He not neglect the wrongdoer but give him respite, and that He not equate the good-doer with the evil-doer, the friend with the enemy, the obedient with the disobedient. It requires that one strive greatly to draw near to Him through obedience, out of gratitude to Him, and that no one turn away from Him, because all things are in His hand and nothing is in the hand of anyone else. Therefore one must fear the severity of His seizure, for the one characterized by generosity is none other than mighty; he is extremely forbearing, and of great force when his sanctity is violated after that forbearance, for he finds many helpers for his purpose, and the one who punishes him finds no excuse for his failing. This is unlike the base person, who finds no helpers and so his seizure is not severe. Thus the denunciation becomes more intense and severe through these two attributes from this aspect. And from another aspect: one should have been ashamed before the Benefactor whose goodness is in no way troubled, so that no command of His is disobeyed and no right owed to Him is neglected. Moreover, in mentioning these two attributes there is an instruction in the argument (talqin al-hujjah). Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "If He were to ask me, I would say: 'The generosity of the Generous and His forbearance deceived me.'" 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Among the generosity of a man is the bad manners of his servants." Imam al-Ghazali, in his explanation of the Names, said: "He is the One who, when He has power, pardons; when He promises, He fulfills; when He gives, He exceeds the limit of hope; He does not care to whom He gives nor how much He gives; when a need is raised to other than Him, He is not pleased; when one turns away, He reproaches and does not exhaust (the matter); whoever takes refuge in Him and seeks shelter with Him is not lost, and He suffices him beyond the need for means and intercessors."

When he mentioned these two attributes, which indicate the two perfections, with majesty (al-jalal), he indicated them by affirming them through the outpouring of generosity in nurture, with the attribute of beauty (al-jamal) through honour (al-ikram), lest a person, because of his rebelliousness, believe that he is free, the owner of himself, doing whatever he wills. So He said: ﴿Who created you﴾ [i.e., brought you into existence] from non-existence, prepared for the shaping of the limbs, ﴿and proportioned you﴾ after those stages, by actually fashioning the limbs and their functions, ﴿and balanced you﴾, i.e., He made each thing of that sound, with the power of its benefits deposited in it for which Allah created it, and He balanced the temperament even before the form. Taswiyah (proportioning) is making the structure proportionate in its creation, and likewise ʿadl (balancing) in the reading of the Kufans with the light pronunciation [i.e., ﴿fa-ʿadalaka﴾ with the lightened ʿ-d-l], [i.e.,] ﴿so He inclined you﴾ away from disfiguring the creation and making the form ugly, and made you well-proportioned in your form. All of this calls for the utmost gratitude and fear of Him should you disobey, for just as He is able to proportion, He is able to disfigure and to other punishments.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 82, verse 8:

When He illuminated by this a light like the sun's light, that He is mighty in power over everything He wills, He produced His saying, linking it to "rakaba" (He assembled): ﴿In whatever form He willed﴾ from among the forms that you know and those that you do not know, of beasts, birds, and other [ of the animals ], and so on. Since the purpose was to establish the meaning to the utmost degree of establishment, He placed the negation within the context of affirmation, so that the opposite of what the speech affirmed would be negated, and the meaning's firmness would reach a degree [ of ] strength beyond which there is no increase. So He said: ﴿Assembled you﴾, meaning: He composed the structure of your limbs and joined the spirit to the body. Al-Tabarani narrated in his three mu'jams (collections of hadith arranged by the names of the transmitters' teachers), with reliable transmitters, from Malik ibn al-Huwayrith, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah, mighty is His name, wills to create a living soul, and a man has intercourse with a woman, his water spreads into every [ vein ] and sinew of hers. When the seventh day comes, Allah brings before him every vein between him and Adam." Then [ he recited ]: ﴿In whatever form He willed He assembled you﴾. From this it becomes clear that the human being is a servant in a binding servitude, and whoever casts off the noose of that binding servitude is left to himself and perishes.

(p-٣٠٥) When Allah, glory be to Him, had made the proof of His power to bring back again by means of the first creation as clear as possible, and had shown that what caused man to suffer loss by forgetting this proof, which points to that abode, was nothing but deception, and since deception is applied to its lightest sense, He showed that it had risen to its peak, saying: ﴿Nay﴾, meaning: what has led you, O people, to turn away from Him to whom turning is obligatory, and whose turning away is extremely ugly, is not merely some kind of delusion ﴿rather﴾ its greatest form, which is that you ﴿deny﴾, meaning continuously and repeatedly, despite the establishment of decisive proofs and the manifest demonstrations, ﴿the Religion﴾, meaning the recompense which Allah appointed [on] the Day of Resurrection. So turn back from delusion entirely, both the particular and the general, and restrain yourselves in the utmost restraint.

"And indeed, over you" — i.e., the situation being that over you (namely, from among those whom We have appointed of Our host, the angels) — "are watchers" — guarding you concerning your deeds, in the utmost degree of exaltedness; so that nothing of them, great or small, is hidden from them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 82, verse 11:

When He had established for them the guarding (ḥifẓ), He cleared them of addition and omission, so He said: ﴿Noble﴾, meaning that they are at the utmost degree of purity of character, chastity, and trustworthiness.

When the guarding and trustworthiness had been established with complete clarity, and the guardian might (p-306) forget, He said: ﴿Recording⁠﴾, meaning that they are firmly rooted in the attribute of writing, writing it down in the scrolls just as the witnesses write down the contracts among you, so that the recompense falls upon the utmost precision in recording.

When elevation (al-isti'la') and the expression by attribute had conveyed the comprehensiveness of their observation of what manifests from deeds, he stated it explicitly, saying: ﴿They know﴾, meaning continually and constantly, ﴿what you do﴾, meaning you renew its doing, of good and evil, with firm resolve and sincere motive, whether it is based on knowledge or not. How, then, could there be, along with this, a denial of recompense for the smallest speck and the thinnest membrane? Would the counting of the weight of atoms of dust among your deeds be in vain? Do you know of a king who has subjects and leaves them neglected, so that he does not hold them accountable for what is in their hands [and what they have done]? And because of their denial of the Religion, he emphasized the meaning that implies it, which is the appointment of the recording guardians (al-hafazah), with the utmost emphasis. The expression in the future tense indicates that they know every thought that arises in the heart and occurs to the mind before one acts. As for what has not passed through the soul [he mentioned], they do not know it, as the hadith clarifies:

"Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, record it for him as a good deed."

Since the outcome of the recording of deeds is the requital for them, this led to a statement of the purpose for which the recording was made, distinguishing the good-doer from the evildoer, a distinction that is not fitting for the wisdom of the Wise nor the generosity of any other Generous, in His saying, by way of emphasis, to refute their denial: ﴿Indeed, the righteous﴾, that is, those who act by what is broadly pleasing to them of what pleases God (p-307), may His power be exalted, ﴿are surely in bliss﴾, that is, enveloped by it, never separated from it, nor they from it, fundamentally: in this world, in the bliss of witnessing (shuhud), and in the Hereafter, in the bliss of vision (ru'yah) and existence, in this abode in meaning and in the Hereafter in sensation. So every bliss in Paradise that is theirs from the deferred gifts has its subtleties (raqa'iq) in this world, which are immediate for them.

Translation of al-Biqa'i's commentary (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 82, verse 14:

﴿Indeed, the wicked (al-fujjar)﴾, that is, those whose nature is to depart from that in which one ought to remain steadfast, from the pleasure of God to His wrath, ﴿are surely in Hellfire (jahim)﴾, that is, a fire that blazes with the utmost blazing, they will be burned by it, the Hellfire of dreadful punishment, just as they were in the world in the Hellfire of distance and severance.

Since the context is one of warning, he described the punishment of the wicked, saying: ﴿They will burn therein﴾, meaning they will be immersed in it like a roasted sheep, so they will be in direct contact with its heat, ﴿on the Day of Judgment (yawm al-Din)﴾, meaning the recompense for deeds that are recorded down to the weight of atoms.

Since punishment, as we are accustomed to it, must come to an end, he made clear that His punishment is of a different kind, so He said: ﴿And they will not be absent from it﴾, meaning, while the state is that they are not ﴿absent from it﴾, that is, from the Blazing Fire (al-Jahim), ﴿absent﴾, meaning, there is no absence from it that could be established for them at any time, but rather they will be therein abiding forever, as a recompense for their deeds, in exact measure, justly and in full correspondence, even now in the abode of this world, although they do not perceive it except after death, because people are asleep, and when they die, they awaken.

When al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) had established that the greatest threat is the Day of Religion (yawm al-din), he magnified its matter by asking about it, to inform that it is worthy that one should devote one's life to attending to its affair and to inquiring into the reality of its state, with the inquiry of faith and submission, not the inquiry of disbelief and rebellion, so that it would be more firmly fixed as a warning concerning it. So He said: ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Religion is?﴾ That is: what will inform you, even if you strive to seek understanding of it? ﴿What is the Day of Religion?﴾ That is: what thing [it is] in its length, its terrors, its severity, and its convulsion.

Since its terrors were beyond all measure, he repeated that question for this state, saying, expressing it with the particle of delay (tarakhi) to increase the awe: ﴿Then what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?﴾ That is, likewise, ﴿what is the Day of Judgment?﴾

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 82, verse 19:

When he had shown that He is of such greatness that the insight of any abode cannot grasp Him, however great it is and however hard it strives, he summarized His matter in an explanation of what the intellects can bear of it, in a general way, repelling what some who have no intellect may say: "If you have joined and sought refuge in some of the great ones, and directed yourself to some of the eminent, then he (the intercessor) may gain you release by force, or by intercession and the like." So he said, substituting from "the Day of Judgment" in the reading of Ibn Kathir and the Basrans in the nominative case: ﴿The Day﴾, which is an adverbial noun of time. Al-Kisa'i said: The Arabs prefer the nominative when they attach "the night" and "the day" to a future (verb), and when they attach them to a past verb they prefer the accusative. ﴿No soul will have power﴾, meaning in no way and at no time, ﴿over another soul﴾, meaning a soul of any kind, without exception. The rest (of the readers) put it in the accusative as an adverbial noun of time. It is permissible that the fatha be for indeclinability, because it is attached to something not fully declinable. ﴿Anything﴾, meaning little or much. Although this day is established, in this abode He, glorified is He, has concealed Himself within the causes, so it is firmly fixed in souls that existing beings harm and benefit because they speak and strike. As for there, what is firmly fixed in souls is the opposite of that, namely that no one speaks except by His permission, an apparent permission, and no one has any action except by His permission in the same way. So the whole matter is always His, but His outward name there is manifest and His inward name is this, which establishes the causes of delusion and is pleasing.

Since the implication was: there is no command for anyone of creation at all, neither outwardly nor inwardly, he followed it with His saying: ﴿And the command﴾, meaning all of it, ﴿that Day﴾, meaning since the resurrection is for recompense, ﴿belongs to Allah﴾, meaning it is exclusively His, no sharer shares in it outwardly, just as no sharer shares in it inwardly. There will occur there the complete unveiling, so no one claims for anyone any matter of affairs without a specific apparent permission, and knowledge becomes necessary through that. Therefore there will be the splitting of the sky and the great earthquakes, and the reckoning of all deeds, small and great, and its end has returned, as you see, to its beginning, and its joint has been wrapped around its connector. And Allah is the Guide to what is right.
